rejected.why: The plant establishes Scrooge conducting business on the day of Marley's funeral, but the payoff only notes Belle's husband seeing Scrooge alone in his office while Marley lay dying, not on the day of Marley's funeral/burial.
The plant beats describe Scrooge refusing to donate and demanding to be left alone, but do not establish the specific remark about decreasing the surplus population.
The plant beats do not mention Scrooge asking about prisons or Union workhouses; they only state that he refuses to donate, demands to be left alone, and dismisses the gentlemen.

accepted.why: Marley warns Scrooge to expect three spirits beginning when the bell tolls one.
Scrooge brandishes a ruler to scare away a boy singing a Christmas carol through his keyhole.
Fred invites Scrooge to come have Christmas dinner with his family, which Scrooge angrily refuses.
Scrooge is terrified when his heavy front door knocker transforms into the spectral face of Marley.
Scrooge turns away the portly gentleman collecting charitable donations for the poor.
The charwoman reveals she stole the curtains right off the dead man's bed while he lay there.
